1.label: very_easy
1.summary: Arrange three colored rods in a 7³ volume. The smaller construction substantially reduces the number of positions, orientations, colors, and projection constraints that must be reconciled.
1.natural_language: Place three colored holographic rods so their front, side, and top dies agree.

2.label: easy
2.summary: Arrange four rods in the same 7³ volume. At least one ray in each die hides a farther rod, introducing the frontmost-color rule while keeping the number of coupled pieces small.
2.natural_language: Place four colored holographic rods so the nearest color in every front, side, and top die agrees.

3.label: medium
3.summary: Arrange five rods with hidden depth rays in every die. Each placement must now be checked against more coupled color and depth constraints across the three views.
3.natural_language: Place five colored holographic rods so the nearest color in every front, side, and top die agrees.

4.label: hard
4.summary: Preserve the original foundry: six rods in a 7³ volume, with at least two genuinely occluded rays in each die. Matching all three frontmost-color masks requires resolving 3D depth, color, and rod orientation together.
4.natural_language: Manipulate the holographic rods until one casting satisfies the front, side, and top shadow dies.

5.label: very_hard
5.summary: Arrange seven rods in an 8³ volume with at least three hidden depth rays in every die. The larger construction combines more possible positions, orientations, colors, and occlusion relationships in every decision.
5.natural_language: Manipulate seven holographic rods until all three frontmost-color shadow dies agree.

simplified.summary: Select a rod and use labelled X, Y, Z, and cycle-axis controls to apply one discrete transform.

full.summary: Select a rod, drag its visible axis handle through one detent to translate it, and drag the orientation ring to cycle its physical rod axis.
